newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev flat, seen stable despite rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev flat, seen stable despite rate cut.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev opened at 1,500-1,510 per dollar, in a wider spread from Thursday's close at 1,504-1,506, and was expected to trade stable despite a cut in the main interest rate, dealers said.
"Banks are testing a wider trading range basically around yesterday's closing levels but trade is thin. The dollar is bid at 1,500-1,504 levs and is offered at 1,507-1,510," one dealer said.
Traders did not expect pressure on the lev to mount following a cut of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) central interest rate to 8.03 percent monthly
"Despite the cut, lev-denominated instruments still provide higher yields than foreign currency investments," another dealer said.
The BNB said on Thursday it would lower the main rate from a current 14.15 percent, effective on Monday, in line with the falling yields of government securities auctioned since last Friday.
